provenance.column_I_caveat: In this block the workbook's comments column is a LOOSE HARDWARE LIST, not row-aligned: I62 (NAS77A4-015) sits on the header row and I64 (MS21299C4K) sits next to 'spherical bearing'. export.note: Established 2026-08-06 by handoff citation_export_provenance. This is the ONLY export of 215197 anywhere in the workspace: all three drawing-checker runs of it record this same sha256 in data/runs.jsonl, 20260730_133912's 215197_A_p01.json records source_pdf '[PRELIM 2025-MAY-22] 215197 A.1.pdf', and no other 215197 PDF exists in drawing-checker's inbox or fixtures. Unlike 217755 (six exports on disk), 'which export' has a unique answer here. This element's own note, unlike its tan_link sibling's, does not name the export it was read on -- so the basis here is uniqueness (there is only one 215197 export for 'sheet 2 zone D10' to refer to), not a written record of the reading.

source_ref.note: 215197 carries TWO 4.06 ±0.10 callouts: '5X 4.06 ±0.10' at sheet 2 zone D10 (perpendicularity 0.05 G, 5X INDIVIDUALLY) and a single '4.06 ±0.10' at sheet 1 zone D5 (positional 0.2 A B C, datum D). The workbook's 3.96/4.16 matches both. This joint is qty 1, which argues for the sheet-1 D5 callout; the tolerance alone cannot decide. Separately, DETAIL X balloons the VPA (1) against the TANGENTIAL LINK MOUNT 215175-002 (72), not the pitch plate 215177-001 -- so 215197 may be the wrong part entirely for this flange.

elements.name: fastener grip (.812 in)
elements.note: 0.812 +/-0.010 in. Workbook row 71 restates the grip with no tolerance; row 73 is the toleranced one and is the row used. RE-CITED 2026-08-06 (handoff traced_labels_and_ratio): the band now comes off the NAS6404 standard, not the parts list.

source_ref.note: One sheet covers NAS6403 through NAS6420: the 'Grip ±.010' column is shared by every basic number, and the per-basic-number columns to its right give overall LENGTH ±.015 (NAS6404 = .2500-28, the .250-28 thread this joint uses; its dash-13 length is 1.182). Sheet 2 CODE block decodes the part number -- dash 13 x .0625 = .8125 -> .812 as printed, 'U' = unplated, 'D' = drilled shank -- and its EXAMPLE OF PART NUMBER block is written against NAS6404 specifically. Sheet 2 note (a) defines grip as underside of head to the end of the full cylindrical shank. WAS `kind: parts_list` / `confidence: traced` citing 217755 balloon 27, whose own note admitted 'the +/-.010 in is untraced (NAS6404 spec absent)'. Which bolt sits in this joint is still the parts list's evidence: NAS6404U13D, find 27 qty 1, ballooned in 217755 sheet 5 DETAIL X. Scan, no text layer -- read by vision from a crop, command in docs/sessions/lessons/LESSONS_20260806_traced_labels_and_ratio.md. MERGE NOTE 2026-08-06 (review/traced_labels_and_ratio): the sibling handoff citation_export_provenance had added a source_ref.export block here naming the 2026-JUL-23 POST export of 217755 by sha256. Dropped deliberately, not lost: it described the parts-list citation this element no longer makes, and `kind: "spec"` is exempt from the export requirement because data/inbox/specs/ is append-only, so the filename already identifies the bytes. The same sha256 is still live on under_head_chamfer_washer in this file.

paths.label: total stack under the fastener grip

checks.label: worst case (MMC+ = max shank out)
checks.guidance: Grip minus the clamped stack. Negative at minimum means the thread run-out is pulled inside the joint; positive at maximum means full-diameter shank protrudes past the nut face. This stack has NO thread-transition allowance, unlike the tan-link take 1.

notes: The as-drawn joint is a castellated nut (MS9363-10, balloon 25) + cotter pin (MS24665-229, balloon 26). Grip length alone cannot answer this joint: the binding constraint is whether a castellation slot lines up with the cotter hole. The workbook does not model it; neither does this transcription.
This stack has no thread-transition element and no second washer branch, so it has strictly less modelling than the tan-link take 1.
